q.t: All the points that are 4 cm from a point P form a …
q.e: A circle is every point at one fixed distance (the radius) from the centre.

q.t: The fixed distance from the centre to the circle is called the …
q.e: The radius is the distance from the centre to any point on the circle.

q.t: Which tool draws a circle?
q.e: The compass point stays at the centre while the pencil keeps a fixed distance.

q.t: In a rectangle, how many angles are 90°?
q.e: Property R2: all four angles of a rectangle are right angles.

q.t: In a rectangle, which sides are equal?
q.e: Property R1: opposite sides are equal.

q.t: A square has …
o: all sides equal and all angles 90°
q.e: Properties S1 and S2.

q.t: A square is turned so it stands on a corner. Is it still a square?
o: Yes — turning doesn't change sides or angles
q.e: Rotation keeps every length and angle the same.

q.t: A line joining opposite corners of a rectangle is called a …
q.e: Diagonals join opposite corners, like AC and BD in ABCD.

q.t: A half circle has radius 2 cm. How long a stretch of line does it cover (end to end)?
q.e: The ends are a diameter apart: 2 × radius = 4 cm.

q.t: Which tool is best for copying an exact length to a new place?
q.e: Set the compass to the length once and it carries it anywhere without re-measuring.

q.t: Which is NOT a valid name for square PQRS (corners in order P, Q, R, S)?
q.e: Names must walk round the corners in order. P → Q → S jumps across the square.

q.t: A wavy line AB is 8 cm long with two equal half-circle waves. What radius does each wave have?
q.e: Each wave covers half the line, 4 cm. That's a diameter, so radius = 2 cm.

q.t: Can a four-sided figure have all angles 90° but opposite sides unequal?
o: No — four right angles force opposite sides to be equal
q.e: With right angles at both ends, the top side is pushed to match the bottom, and the sides to match each other.

q.t: In a rectangle, the two diagonals are …
q.e: Both diagonals of a rectangle have the same length.

q.t: A diagonal splits a rectangle's corner into two parts. They always add up to …
q.e: Together they make the whole corner, which is a right angle.

q.t: A diagonal splits a corner into 40° and one other angle. What is the other?
q.e: The two parts make the 90° corner: 90 − 40 = 50°.

q.t: A diagonal splits the corners into 45° and 45°. The rectangle must be a …
q.e: The diagonal splits the corner equally only when the two sides at that corner are equal.

q.t: A rectangle must split into 2 identical squares. If the breadth is 4 cm, the length is …
q.e: Two squares of side 4 cm side by side: length = 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

q.t: Where should the centre of a circular hole be placed to sit exactly in the middle of a square?
o: At the middle of one side
q.e: The crossing point of the diagonals is equally far from all four corners and all four sides.

q.t: A four-sided figure has all sides equal but no right angles. It is a …
q.e: Equal sides alone don't make a square — it also needs 90° angles.

q.t: Rectangle ABCD has AB = 7 cm, BC = 4 cm. X is on AD and Y on BC, both 1 cm from A and B. What is XY?
q.e: Same distance down both sides makes ABYX a rectangle, so XY = AB = 7 cm.

q.t: In that rectangle, when is XY the LONGEST?
o: When X and Y are at opposite corners — XY is a diagonal
When both are at the top
q.e: Corner to opposite corner (X at A, Y at C, or X at D, Y at B) gives the diagonal, the longest distance.

q.t: In that rectangle, what is the SHORTEST XY can be?
q.e: AD and BC are 7 cm apart. Straight across (7 cm) is shortest; any slant is longer.

q.t: A rectangle splits into 3 identical squares and its breadth is 2 cm. What is its length?
q.e: Three squares of side 2 cm in a row: 3 × 2 = 6 cm.

q.t: Which rectangle can NOT be split into two identical squares?
q.e: The length must be exactly twice the breadth. 2 × 2.5 = 5, not 4.

q.t: House: point A must be 5 cm from both B and C. How do you find it with a compass?
o: Draw 5 cm arcs from B and from C; A is where they cross
Measure 5 cm straight up from the middle of BC
Guess and check with a ruler
q.e: Points 5 cm from B lie on one circle, points 5 cm from C on another; A is on both.

q.t: Constructing a rectangle with side 4 cm and diagonal 8 cm: what radius do you set for the arc from A?
q.e: The arc from A must hit the perpendicular at B exactly 8 cm from A — the diagonal's length.

q.t: In a rectangle with side 4 cm, could a diagonal be 3 cm long?
o: No — a diagonal is always longer than a side
Only if the other side is 1 cm
q.e: The diagonal slants across the corner, so it's longer than either side it joins.

q.t: Why keep the compass at one fixed opening when constructing a square?
o: All sides must be equal, and one opening guarantees it
q.e: Re-measuring each side invites small errors; one fixed setting gives exactly equal sides.

q.t: Which shows equal sides on a rough sketch?
o: A small tick '|' on each equal side
q.e: The book's convention: matching tick marks mean equal lengths.

q.t: The roof point A is 5 cm from B and C. Then an arc of radius 5 cm centred at A will …
o: pass through both B and C
q.e: B and C are both exactly 5 cm from A, so they lie on the circle of radius 5 cm around A.

q.t: A tilted square on dot paper has every side going '2 across, 1 up' (turned each time). What does that tell you?
q.e: The same step for every side means the same length every time.

q.t: A rectangle's diagonal makes 50° with the longer side at a corner. What angle does it make with the shorter side?
q.e: The two parts add to the 90° corner.

q.t: In a long thin rectangle, which part of the corner made by the diagonal is SMALLER?
o: The part next to the long side
The part next to the short side
q.e: The diagonal leans towards the long side, so it makes a smaller angle with it.

q.t: How many different valid names (starting point and direction) does a rectangle ABCD have?
q.e: Start at any of 4 corners and go either of 2 ways: 4 × 2 = 8 (ABCD, BCDA, CDAB, DABC and the reverses).

q.t: To construct a rhombus with sides 5 cm, after drawing two sides from a corner, how do you find the fourth corner?
o: Arcs of 5 cm from the two free ends; it's where they cross
q.e: The fourth corner must be 5 cm from both free ends — the same two-arc trick as the house.

q.t: A rectangle 8 cm long splits into how many identical squares if its breadth is 2 cm?
q.e: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 squares of side 2 cm in a row.

q.t: Why does the diagonal split a square's corner into 45° and 45°?
o: The two sides at the corner are equal, so the diagonal sits exactly between them
Because 45 is half of 90 in any rectangle
q.e: Equal adjacent sides make the diagonal lean equally towards both, so the 90° corner is halved.

q.t: X on AD is 2 cm from A and Y on BC is 2 cm from B in a 7 cm × 4 cm rectangle ABCD. What shape is ABYX?
o: A rhombus that isn't a rectangle
q.e: XY is parallel to AB and 7 cm long, with right angles at A and B — a rectangle.

q.t: Which details fix a rectangle exactly (as constructed in the book)?
q.e: Side + right angle + a diagonal arc pins down the far corner. One side or the diagonal alone allows many rectangles.
